note: This session's own read of the 14 rendered crops (2 of 16 sampled were refused by the frame control -- see 2.6g-owner-not-read-manifest.json's `refused`). Kept separate from Sean's own VERDICT_none_yet slot in that manifest, precedent `session_read_2026_09_29` (2.6d.3, 2.6c.3). Categories per the brief: (a) printed ledger lines exist and BOTH readers missed them; (b) no ledger lines printed and the note sits at a distance an engraver would print one -- the far threshold may be wrong; (c) not a note / not a real contest; (d) other / inconclusive on this ink.

readings.subject: glyph/10/1/8/8/6
readings.note: Small isolated blob in the gap beside an 'ff' mark; left/right overhangs read ~0 at every step -- genuinely blank paper either side, no ledger of any kind. Could equally be a stray mark rather than a note; not confident enough to call (c).

readings.subject: glyph/10/1/10/0/1
readings.note: Subject sits inside a dense beamed 8th/16th run; step1 has center=0.987 AND adjacent=0.743 -- everything in the band is dense, consistent with beam/chord ink rather than an isolated thin rung. Cannot tell by eye whether a rung is fused in.

readings.subject: glyph/11/1/10/15/1
readings.note: Two stems bracket the head; text ('esc.', likely the tail of a 'cresc.' running into the crop margin) sits above. No clean horizontal stroke visible through the dense ink. Plausibly a real note whose ledger (if any) is fused with the stems -- not confirmable at this zoom.

readings.subject: glyph/4/1/0/1/0
readings.note: Isolated blob near a tuplet '3'; overhangs low/mixed, no visible ledger line. Looks like a real note sitting alone with nothing printed under/over it.

readings.subject: glyph/2/0/2/1/7
readings.note: The RED bracket sits on the 'c' of the printed word 'cresc.' -- this is direction text, not a note. Exactly the shape FINDINGS §2.6c.2 named for Litolff glyph/8/0/6/12/7 (the 's' of 'sempre').

readings.subject: glyph/7/0/2/6/2
readings.note: Chord cluster; one step reads left=0.94 dense but right=0.16 not dense (or the mirror) at every step that is at all elevated -- classic ONE-SIDED asymmetry, i.e. a neighbour's own ink reaching into the window on that side only, not a rung reaching past the head on BOTH sides.

readings.subject: glyph/8/1/7/3/2
readings.note: Extremely dense cluster of overlapping stems (Litolff MERGING at its worst in this sample); the subject itself is barely distinguishable from the surrounding ink. Not classifiable by eye.

readings.subject: glyph/8/1/2/18/1
readings.note: Isolated blob between the staves under a slur; left=right=0.0 at every step except the head's own centre -- truly blank paper on both sides. No ledger printed at the distance (expected 2-3 rungs) this note is filed at.

readings.subject: glyph/10/1/10/8/3
readings.note: Near an 'ff'; one step's left=0.52 sits just under the 0.55 DENSE floor while right=0.31 does not -- an asymmetric near-miss, more consistent with adjacent ink than a clean rung, but close enough to flag.

readings.subject: glyph/10/0/7/1/2
readings.note: The CLOSEST near-miss of the 14: center=0.719 dense, right=0.508 just under the 0.55 floor, and adjacent=0.375 just OVER the 0.35 ceiling -- all three guards miss this window by a small margin in the SAME direction a real, slightly-thick or slightly-off-grid rung would. This is the one crop where I would guess a real rung is more likely than not, and both readers missed it on threshold, not on absence.

readings.subject: glyph/10/1/10/0/6
readings.note: Isolated head; one step's right=0.715 dense while left=0.06 is not -- one-sided again, likely the neighbouring run's ink to the right, not an independent ledger.

readings.subject: glyph/13/0/2/6/4
readings.note: Dense passage but the tested steps read near-zero on both overhangs except the head's own centre; no ledger visible through the surrounding ink at this zoom.

readings.subject: glyph/4/1/6/5/6
readings.note: Under a slur in a beamed run; one step shows left=0.33/right=0.76 (asymmetric, right dense) -- reads as neighbour ink again, not confirmable as a rung.

readings.subject: glyph/4/1/7/3/2
readings.note: Dense passage, asymmetric overhangs (right elevated at one step, left at another, never both together) -- the recurring one-sided-neighbour-ink shape, not a clean rung.

headline: 0 of 14 show an unambiguous printed ledger line missed by both readers on symmetric evidence. 1 (crop 10) is a genuine near-miss where the detector's own thresholds fall just short in the direction a real rung would push them. 1 (crop 05) is confirmed NOT a note (direction text, the 'cresc.' shape already named in §2.6c.2). The rest split between isolated notes with truly blank paper on both sides (4, category b) and dense/merged passages where a one-sided density reading is more consistent with a NEIGHBOUR's own ink than an independent rung (8, category d) -- never a case of a clean, symmetric rung both readers missed.
